 Denver weather: Rain tapers off as temperatures stay cool
 By Chase Rogers 
 Published November 3, 2026 7:12am 
 + 
 Add Denver Gazette on Google
 The Capital Building stands in downtown Denver on a gloomy, cloudy day. (Emily Bejarano/The Denver Gazette) 
 ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT 
 Denver will stay cool and mostly dry this week, with the last forecasted chance of rain on Tuesday morning.
 The National Weather Service said to expect a high of 57 degrees with a 20% chance of rain in the early morning and a sunny afternoon.

 Wind speeds are expected to be elevated, particularly further east, reaching up to 45 miles per hour.
 Mountain areas could experience some areas of slick driving early in the day. Precipitation is also a possibility on Wednesday in those higher-elevation areas only.
 ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT 
 Expect temperatures to stay just under 60 degrees for the remainder of the week, with no more precipitation likely.
 Tonight, expect a low of 35 degrees with winds calming down a touch.
